question: The construction of an onshore regasification plant in Porto Empedocle, close to the Valley of the Temples in Agrigento, raises questions concerning not only the protection of cultural and environmental heritage but also the EU’s energy planning.

The project, which was classified as strategic under Decree-Law No 181 of 9 December 20231, may not be in keeping with the EU objectives of protecting cultural heritage (Directive 2001/42/EC) and protecting neighbouring Natura 2000 areas (Directive 92/43/EEC), the objectives of the European Green Deal and state aid legislation.

The EU’s energy planning is turning out to be very chaotic, given that there are already energy corridors for Sicily, such as the Argo and Cassiopea gas fields, the link to an onshore treatment and compression plant, and the pipelines linking Sicily with Libya2 and Algeria3 and with Malta4.

Given the presence of a regasification plant in Malta and the end of the emergency concerning ‘reasonably priced’ gas supplies5, and taking into account that the project has been the subject of questions since 20086: 1.
What steps will the Commission take to ensure that the project conforms to EU environmental, energy and state aid legislation7?
Is the project in keeping with the EU’s efforts to safeguard energy security, to diversify sources with a view to environmental sustainability, and to protect cultural heritage?
Supporter8
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (30.4.2024) Launched in May 2022, REPowerEU is helping the EU save energy, produce clean energy, diversify its energy supplies, notably with targeted infrastructure investments to enhance the resilience of our energy system without inhibiting the transition to a climate neutral economy.
Liquefied natural gas (LNG) contributes to the supply diversification of the EU together with pipeline imports, and it is common that pipelines and LNG terminals are in the same area.

Regarding the compliance with EU regulations, including EU environmental law, national authorities are primarily responsible for their full and correct application, including Directives 2011/92/EU1, 2012/18/EU2, 2001/42/EC3 and 92/43/EEC4. It is thus for the Italian authorities to assess and authorise the project by respecting the environmental requirements.

As regards EU competition law, it is for the Member State to assess if a measure may entail the granting of State aid and, if this is the case, to notify it to the Commission. The Commission did not receive a State aid notification for this project. Diversification is a key aspect of Commission action to strengthen EU security of gas supply.
Since 2022, LNG imports have notably contributed to reducing the dependence of Italy on Russian gas.
